newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber says Thai default bad for prices.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber says Thai default bad for prices.

text.p: The decision by the Thai government to default on taking delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber will further depress prices of RSS3 grade rubber, dealers in the Singapore rubber market said on Thursday.

Thailand Deputy Prime Minister Sukhawich Rangsitphol announced late on Thursday that Bangkok will not take delivery of the rubber to trim losses on an official scheme to prop up domestic rubber prices.
"This is not good news for the market. This will surely hit the price of RSS3 rubber, which will probably go down as a result," one trader said.
"The trade was hearing talk about this. I think the reason for this is that they don't have the money and they have problems because of the currency fluctuations," a dealer said.
The Thai baht and other Southeast Asian currencies have been hammered for weeks by a selling spree which has knocked off a large chunk of their value against the U.S. dollar.
Modest shortcovering was seen today in the Singapore rubber market for TSR20 rubber. Traders said Michelin made inquiries for RSS3 rubber, but no deals were said to have been concluded.
At 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 94.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 92.00 cents. -- Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
